title: Krishna beside every one
hookLine: the gopis search the moonlit forest, sing by the river, and Krishna returns to each of them
carry: Krishna is wholly beside each devotee
tomorrow: who rides into the village with a trap from the king?

lines: THE SEARCH, THE SONG, THE CIRCLE.
cards: Have you seen him? The gopis are asking the trees. They go from one to the next in the moonlit forest, a fig, a tulsi plant, a jasmine vine, asking whether he passed this way.
Nobody answers. A moment ago they were sure they were the luckiest women alive. Now they're searching the forest floor for a footprint.

teach.h: FOOTPRINTS, AND A WOMAN'S BESIDE THEM.
teach.b: They do find footprints, his, and beside them a woman's. He has taken one gopi with him. But she grows proud too, asks him to carry her, and he vanishes from her as well.
The others find her weeping alone, and now they're all in the same place: together, without him.
So they go down to the bank of the Yamuna and sing. Tradition calls their song the Gopi Gita.
It has a reproach or two, but mostly it's a long remembering, his walk, his flute, his face coming home with the cows at dusk, and running through it, the plain plea to show himself.
Then he's there, smiling, a garland around his neck. He tells them he stepped away so their love would deepen, the way a poor man who finds treasure and loses it thinks of nothing else.
Then the one they worship says something startling: he can't repay them. Only then does the dance itself happen, the rasa.
The women form a circle, and Krishna appears between every two of them, so each one feels him at her side.

teach.h: NOT A SHARE OF HIM. ALL OF HIM.
teach.b: Not a share of him. All of him, beside each one. Devotees take this as a picture of how God loves: wholly, each soul as if it were the only one.
In Braj, many temples keep the autumn full moon, Sharad Purnima, as the night of this dance.
And the Bhagavata closes with one more frame: whoever hears this with faith gains devotion and is freed from the craving that troubles the heart.

how: Devotees recite and sing the Gopi Gita from the Bhagavata, and the circle dance with Krishna between every two gopis is painted, sung, and performed in Ras Lila dance dramas.

games.q: you're a gopi. you've searched the forest, asked the trees, found footprints, and he's still gone. what do you do?
o: sit with the others by the river and sing your memories of him.
games.why: they go to the Yamuna bank and sing the Gopi Gita, a long remembering, and Krishna appears among them.

practice: The gopis found him again by remembering him together in song, not by searching harder.
If you pray, hum or softly sing one of Krishna's names, Govinda or Gopala, the way people do in kirtan, and picture yourself in the circle with him right beside you, not far off at the center.
If you don't, bring back one moment you felt completely seen by someone, and stay with the details: where you were, the light, a sound.
